summary: Design model of ChecksHub admission: all 11 frozen properties hold at the stated bounds (largest run 780,342 states), all 15 matrix runs end as expected, 24 of 24 mutations detected; one design limit (F1): a lower-lane hosted job can take the account's last place while a release macOS job waits.

modeled: start: refuse while paused, reuse a green digest, hold and supersede
the pump: lane then arrival, place recorded before the dispatch
dispatch answer, run end, cancel landing
leases: lapse, sweep, no late renew
abstracted: one macOS pool and one hosted pool under the account limit, one heavy pool
one shared key group and one shared digest group
no clock: a lease lapses at any moment
assumptions: A1 one admission step at a time
A2 the place is in the ledger before the dispatch await
A3 outside jobs counted at once (code lags one poll)
A4 a dispatch is answered and a run ends
A5 lane, pool, key, digest fixed at start

findings.title: A lower-lane Linux job can take the account's last hosted place while a release macOS job waits
findings.story: An outside macOS run holds the only macOS place (5 of 5 in real terms). A release macOS job arrives and waits for macOS. A land job for Linux arrives, has room in the account and is admitted: no rule is broken, because the release job could not use any free place. The account is now full (40 of 40). When the macOS run ends, the release job still cannot start until a lower-lane Linux job ends. The model reaches this at depth 5 (OutsideStarts, Start release, Start land, Admit land). It is a property of the design's rule (design 5: a free place goes to the first entry that can use it), not a code bug: there is no code. Strict head-of-line would prevent it and is shown wrong by mutation strict-head-of-line (it breaks FirstInLineCanStart). Options for the owner: accept (the 40 cap is far from today's use), reserve the account's last places for release while one waits, or count a waiting release macOS job against the account.
